panel.summary: No blocking defect. Confidence ~85%. Residual non-blocking risks: poll_decision has_etag=False case not pinned by an oracle; annotated-tag peeling verified only on git 2.47.3, other versions could differ; cache-key content hashing is linear in ref count and gated only as 'does not grow faster than the data', not wall-clock bounded, and on network filesystems the 60s max-age plus attribute caching could hold staleness for the full backstop; ETag matching covers a single If-None-Match value, comma-separated lists may miss 304s. Contracts are unusually precise; security ordering (auth before conditional handling, slug resolution against a known set) is correct.

No blocking defect found; confidence high. Four non-blocking issues. Medium: TOCTOU in cache KEY COMPUTATION itself — a file disappearing between path-listing and statting could raise an unhandled FileNotFoundError; should be caught and treated as a forced cache miss. Low: cache-key cost can grow with non-karta refs, since growth fixtures vary only karta refs. Low: hub-mode effective staleness moves from ~5s to ~65s because the new 60s cache sits underneath RepoEngine's 5s cache. Low: poll_decision edge cases (False,False) and (False,True,False) untested. The binder is remarkably thorough and self-adversarial; eight prior rounds are evident in its pre-emptive handling of all-or-nothing batching, same-tick mtime, loose-to-packed transitions, tag peeling, hook write-back and auth-before-conditional. None of the four would cause incorrect behaviour.

No blocking defect. Confidence ~75% at plan level. Residual: (1) High — asymmetric same-tick protection: the content-hash requirement is scoped to ref files, but binder JSONs are keyed on path+size+mtime only, so an in-place same-size same-tick binder edit is invisible until the 60s backstop; self-healing and rare, so non-blocking, but should be hashed too or explicitly accepted in the build report. (2) Medium — the key is over-broad: it hashes every loose ref under refs/ plus packed-refs per request while derivation reads only refs/karta/, refs/heads/karta/ and the default branch. (3) Low — alternates refusal does not cover partial/promisor clones. Both round-eight fixes are correctly applied; contracts and oracles are internally consistent. Ship, with (1) noted.

Verdict: no blocking defect, confidence high. The binder is mechanically consistent: the fixed-call-count claim is scoped to ref queries inside gather_git_facts while the per-request total including default-branch resolution is asserted elsewhere; the path-traversal oracle for the optional detail route is explicit and complete; thread-safety, content-hash, path-set, lock-file exclusion, never-cache-failures and HEAD-as-symref resolution all carry pinned oracles. House patterns (mirrored pure functions, hub auth ordering, _inert_json, injectable runner, atomic sampling) are correctly applied. Four residual items — medium: thread-safety and never-cache-failures interaction under-specified at contract level; low: detached-HEAD cache-key wording, benchmark SIGKILL cleanup note, HEAD-as-probe rationale — are implementer-discipline issues the oracles catch, not design flaws. Ship.

panel.verdict: no blocking defect at the binder level (8/10)
panel.summary: No blocking defect at the binder level. The earlier contradictions are fixed, and the oracle covers the main auth, traversal, cache-invalidation, failure-degradation and call-count regressions. Residual risks, not blockers: cache wording should explicitly require content hashes for packed-refs and the resolved HEAD target, not just loose refs; archived-payload budget versus file:// snapshot can conflict if inline archived summaries are large; the benchmark should clean all GIT_* variables and neutralise copied config and worktree metadata, not only the four named; client visibility behaviour is source-verified, not browser-proven. Confidence 8/10 that this binder can be committed as a contract, 6/10 on runtime correctness without seeing the final implementation.
